ai.definition: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is a method of securely distributing cryptographic keys using principles of quantum mechanics to ensure that any interception or unauthorized access can be detected.
ai.howItWorks: QKD uses entangled particles such as photons to transmit information. Any attempt by an eavesdropper to intercept the communication will alter the state of these particles, which can be detected at the receiving end, thus ensuring the security of the key exchange.
ai.problemSolved: Traditional encryption methods are vulnerable to quantum computing attacks that could potentially break current cryptographic systems. QKD provides a solution by leveraging quantum mechanics to ensure secure and unbreakable communication channels.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing QKD devices involves creating highly precise optical components, such as lasers and detectors, which need to operate at low temperatures and in controlled environments to maintain their functionality.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes designing and fabricating quantum optics, integrating them into a secure communication system, and calibrating the entire setup for optimal performance. This involves complex engineering and stringent quality control measures.
ai.costDrivers: High costs are driven by the need for specialized materials, low-temperature environments, and the complexity of integration with existing communication infrastructure.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: While still in its early stages, QKD is expected to see widespread adoption as quantum computing threats become more imminent. The technology is currently being tested in various real-world scenarios.
ai.regulation: There are no specific regulations for QKD at present, but the technology will likely be subject to cybersecurity and data protection laws once it becomes mainstream.
ai.risks: Technical challenges include maintaining the stability of quantum states over long distances and ensuring secure integration with existing networks. There is also a risk that advancements in quantum computing could render current QKD systems obsolete.
ai.profitability: The market for QKD is expected to grow as organizations prioritize data security, but profitability will depend on overcoming technical hurdles and achieving broader adoption.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will focus on improving the distance over which secure keys can be distributed without loss of quality, reducing costs, and integrating QKD with existing communication systems.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking. Long-term operation requires stable power supplies and cooling systems.

glossary.def: A phenomenon in quantum mechanics where particles become interconnected such that the state of one particle can instantaneously affect the state of another, no matter the distance between them.
A communication channel based on principles of quantum mechanics used to transmit information securely through QKD.

subsystems.name: Photon source
subsystems.role: generates the quantum states (single photons or weak coherent pulses) that carry the key.

subsystems.name: Quantum channel
subsystems.role: transmits photons with minimal loss and disturbance between the two parties.

subsystems.name: Detector
subsystems.role: measures incoming photons and records their quantum state.

subsystems.name: Classical authenticated channel
subsystems.role: public link used for basis reconciliation, error correction and authentication.

subsystems.name: Post-processing
subsystems.role: turns raw detection events into a shared secret key and estimates eavesdropping.

subsystems.name: Key management
subsystems.role: stores keys and supplies them to encryption devices on demand.

buildSteps.title: Survey the link
buildSteps.detail: Measure distance and loss; choose optical fibre for metropolitan links or free-space/satellite for longer or mobile paths.

buildSteps.title: Install endpoints
buildSteps.detail: Set up photon sources and single-photon detectors at each end, with precise timing and alignment.

buildSteps.title: Establish classical authentication
buildSteps.detail: Set up an authenticated public channel so an eavesdropper cannot impersonate either party.

buildSteps.title: Transmit quantum signals
buildSteps.detail: Send photons one by one (or as weak pulses) and record which detector fires and at what time.

buildSteps.title: Sift the raw key
buildSteps.detail: Compare measurement bases over the classical channel and keep only the events where both sides used the same basis.

buildSteps.title: Correct errors and check security
buildSteps.detail: Run error correction to reconcile differences; estimate the error rate to bound how much an eavesdropper might know.

buildSteps.title: Amplify privacy
buildSteps.detail: Compress the corrected key into a shorter string that is provably secret except with negligible probability.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with encryption
buildSteps.detail: Feed the key into a classical encryptor (one-time pad or AES) for data transmission.

buildSteps.title: Operate and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Continuously generate fresh keys and watch for anomalies that could indicate an attack or hardware fault.

prerequisites.why: they must detect individual photons with low noise and high timing resolution.

prerequisites.tech: Low-loss optical fibre or free-space links
prerequisites.why: fibre loss limits range to a few hundred kilometres without repeaters; free-space needs clear line of sight.
keys must be based on true randomness, not pseudo-random algorithms.
the classical channel must be authenticated without relying on unproven computational assumptions.
they would extend entanglement-based QKD beyond the reach of direct fibre or trusted-node networks.
interoperability and security certification are still maturing, slowing large-scale deployment.

pathway.milestone: Metropolitan point-to-point QKD links and small trusted-node networks
pathway.unlocks: high-security key exchange for banks, data centres and government links over tens to hundreds of kilometres.

pathway.milestone: National trusted-node backbones and satellite QKD for intercontinental key exchange
pathway.unlocks: wider coverage without quantum repeaters, though each trusted node must be physically secure.
long-distance QKD without trusted nodes, plus building blocks for a quantum internet.

pathway.milestone: Integration with quantum-safe cryptography and quantum networks
pathway.unlocks: hybrid systems that combine physics-based key distribution with post-quantum algorithms for defence in depth.
